As much as I appreciate the quality of this video, I think it’s a misconception and perhaps delusion to think about LLMs in terms of just ‘yet another tool’. It’s a new form of intelligence, which seems to be capable to make human level of intelligence essentially a commodity. Meaning, that if all the tasks you do at your job are essentially providing intelligence (software development is one of those), it can be replaced by a LLM. In this case saying ‘AI cannot replace your job’ is akin to saying ‘car cannot replace your horse’. But it did.

The most important thing missing from this analysis is that the technological improvement has to come in a field and a time where there is enormous unmet demand. At the time, there was massive unmet demand for - Software and websites - Movies and TV - Consumer plane travel Is there still enormous unmet demand for software? Or has the iPhone stayed the same for 5 years, people hate the seventh UI re-design of that website, all software companies are making the same short-form content app that people wish they used less, VR was rejected, etc. Is there still enormous demand for TV and movies, or do people already feel like there is too much to watch in a lifetime? Will people continue to want to travel as every popular spot become ever more saturated with crowds of tourists who can now afford to visit a different city every day? As we are seeing human lifespan, birth rates, and self-reported happiness peak and decline in developed countries, we must question the long-held assumption that the outputs we produce are valuable rather than harmful to human beings. Until we know the outputs are helpful, we should actively reject the acceleration of efficiency and productivity. What people need today is not more money, but a sense of self-worth, community, meaning, relief from anxiety, a smaller, quieter world that they can comprehend, where they can feel peace of mind and operate effectively. There is no evidence AI will help create these things.
